hints: Recall the SI base units for mass and thermodynamic temperature.
Give the unit names or their accepted symbols: kg for mass and K for temperature.
walkthrough: The stated units already cover electric current (ampere), length (metre) and time (second).
Two other SI base quantities in the syllabus are mass and thermodynamic temperature.
Their base units are kilogram (kg) and kelvin (K).

ai_rubric.observable: States kilogram or kg as an SI base unit.
States kelvin or K as an SI base unit.

hints: Rearrange the equation to make μ the subject, then write the units of every quantity in SI base units.
Use [v] = m s⁻¹, [F] = kg m s⁻² and [e] = A s before cancelling common factors.
walkthrough: Rearrange v = μF/e to μ = ve/F.
The base units are [v] = m s⁻¹, [F] = kg m s⁻² and [e] = A s because charge equals current multiplied by time.
Substitute the units: [μ] = (m s⁻¹)(A s)/(kg m s⁻²).
Cancel m and combine the powers of s to obtain [μ] = A kg⁻¹ s².
